channel.title: Noticias del Mundo — Ciencia
channel.description: Noticias de ciencia de todas las fuentes configuradas.

item.title: Workplace absenteeism: Why temporary disability is a right, not an expense
item.description: Temporary disability is a cornerstone of the public Social Security system. It is a right for all workers who fall ill and a social security benefit designed primarily to protect those who are sick, enabling them to receive medical treatment and recover or improve their condition while ensuring they have sufficient income during periods in which they are unable to work. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New light-conversion tool could help speed up quantum computing
item.description: Want to break down some basics in the world of quantum research over dinner? Researchers at the Cockrell School of Engineering have you covered. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI has solved a host of big math problems—here's why this threatens the whole field of mathematics
item.description: For many, the year 2026 will be remembered as the one when mathematics had an identity crisis and forever changed. Frontier (cutting-edge) AI models made by OpenAI and Anthropic made stunning progress on hundreds of open problems that have baffled mathematicians for decades—and centuries in some cases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Do a violin's physical characteristics really improve with regular playing?
item.description: There is a widespread notion among violinists: A violin "opens up" as it is played, which is to say its sound gradually improves. However, an experiment conducted by a team led by a CNRS researcher has challenged this belief in a study published in Acta Acustica. After six months, the professional soloist in charge of playing the violin judged the process complete, reporting that the instrument had become easier to play and its tone had improved. Yet, no physical or acoustic measurement confirmed that this feeling resulted from such a mechanical change in the instrument itself. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genetic mosaic helps explain diverse forms of Darwin's finches
item.description: Darwin's finches are known for their varied beaks, which help them take advantage of different food sources in the Galápagos Islands. Much previous research has focused on seed-eating ground finches, but their relatives that search for insects in forested areas have received less attention. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Recipe for one of the world's most important cancer drugs uncovered: Tobacco plants could produce the medicine
item.description: More people around the world will receive a cancer diagnosis at some point in their lives. As this trend is expected to continue, researchers have been working to crack the code of how the widely used cancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel) is naturally produced, with the aim of making its production cheaper and more efficient in the future. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Robert Macfarlane says trust in Cop to deliver change on climate is ‘misplaced’
item.description: Nature writer reveals in his first Reith lecture that he finds ‘much more hope’ in emerging alliances We are “misplacing our trust” in the Cop climate summits and their “capacity to deliver consequential change”, according to Robert Macfarlane in this year’s Reith lectures. In comments recorded before this week’s failure of the 31st UN climate summit to deliver an agreement on action to combat global heating , the bestselling author said he saw “much more hope” in emerging alliances such as the Santa Marta process , which is a smaller group of countries committed to phasing out fossil fuels… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Barkham

item.title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs
item.description: A quantum device with more qubits is harder to verify. Describing a general quantum state takes an exponential number of parameters, and reconstructing it in full—a procedure known as state tomography—becomes impractical as the system grows. Yet most experiments do not need the full description. They need to know a few things: Is the state close to the target? Are the qubits entangled? And does the system carry the resources needed for quantum computation? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses
item.description: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. A new study by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) uncovers the inner workings of the poxvirus core: how its gene-copying machines sit parked in dormant pairs, ready to print viral instructions and release them into the host cell through dedicated export portals embedded in the core shell. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful
item.description: Most online shoppers know that ads strategically follow them across sites, a mechanism known as "ad retargeting." A new study led by Penn State researchers found that consumers find these targeted ads helpful, but explaining why they are seeing an ad can backfire by increasing concerns about being watched. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA spacecraft data reveal how solar system's tail shifts over 14 years
item.description: A Southwest Research Institute-led study is the first to map out the distinct motion paths of the heliotail lobes across a 14-year period using data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft. By identifying the paths followed by these lobes, the study provides a better understanding of how solar activity shapes the heliotail. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs fluid flow from sparse, noisy data
item.description: Medical imaging technologies have transformed how scientists and physicians visualize blood flowing through the human heart, but even the most advanced imaging techniques cannot capture every detail of fluid motion. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine, have developed a computational approach that combines fundamental physics with artificial intelligence to reconstruct a more complete and accurate picture of fluid flow from limited and imperfect measurements. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Overlooked symmetry group offers new geometric blueprint for the Standard Model and topologically protected vacuums
item.description: For more than half a century, physicists searching for a grand unified theory have followed one unspoken rule: go bigger. If you want to weave nature's fundamental forces into a single mathematical framework, the classic recipe says you need a giant "simple" symmetry group—structures like SU(5) or SO(10) that act like massive algebraic warehouses large enough to hold every force at once. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A hidden link between a flower's color and its scent revealed
item.description: Researchers discovered that the biological machinery behind flower color also helps shape fragrance. By disrupting a single gene in petunias, they changed the flowers' mix of scent compounds, increasing some associated with vanilla and cloves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: South Africa's small cattle farmers need help before super El Niño hits: How to set up shade, water and feed
item.description: In South Africa, more than 2 million smallholder households make a living through agriculture. Within this small-scale farming sector, roughly 613,000 families own cattle. They farm on shared rural rangelands. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nanoparticles repair mitochondria to boost bone regeneration in diabetic rats
item.description: A complication of diabetes is that damaged bones don't heal well, but a group of researchers is helping solve the problem with a novel mechanism to help bone regeneration. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Collapse of U.N. summit intensifies calls for new approach to climate talks
item.description: The failure of COP31 after a dispute about whether a fossil fuel phaseout could even be mentioned has prompted calls for a system that relies less heavily on consensus. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Marina Dias

item.title: Webb finds evidence star's layers may have merged just hours before Cas A supernova
item.description: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Africa disappointed with COP31 outcome
item.description: In tonight's edition, the COP31 climate summit in Turkey has failed to reach an agreement, exposing deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Also, DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi and Kenya's William Ruto agree to restore relations and boost regional cooperation. And determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into a sensory room. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

item.title: Bacteria and nuclear power could grow ready-made homes on Mars before astronauts arrive
item.description: As we gear up to eventually land a human on Mars, more and more ideas are coming out about how to prepare for that. A recent one from Pioneer Labs, a research institute founded by bioengineer Erika DeBenedictis to develop biological technologies for space exploration, is now available on the arXiv preprint server, without any plans to release it in a paid journal as part of the "Open Science" policy of The Astera Institute. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hera surveys asteroids with superhuman vision
item.description: The European Space Agency's Hera mission for planetary defense surveys its target asteroids with a combination of instruments, peering beyond the limits of the human eye. The larger Didymos asteroid—dominated by its dramatic equatorial ridge—is seen here from just 28.5 km (17.7 miles) away, variously in visible light, multispectral and thermal infrared vision. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Data center policy review reveals 'chaotic' patchwork of rules across all 50 states
item.description: The artificial intelligence boom has brought with it debates about where the data centers that run the technology will be located, how big they will be and how to ensure communities benefit from them. Underlying these debates is the question of whether state and local governments should ban them outright, welcome them with open arms or choose something in between. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Satellite observations show how rain breaks up Earth's natural sunshades
item.description: Delivering on its promise, the European Space Agency's EarthCARE satellite is already yielding new insights into the role that clouds play in regulating Earth's climate. The latest findings shed light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright cloud formations that help keep our planet cool—with rain emerging as a key driver. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Some people claim to speak many languages. But what does it really mean to be a polyglot?
item.description: Roughly half of the world's population speaks more than one language. But speaking two or three languages is very different from claiming proficiency in five, 10 or more. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Las imágenes satelitales de la NASA que muestran cómo El Niño transformó al desierto de Atacama
item.description: La agencia espacial registró una floración histórica en el norte de Chile; el fenómeno climático transformó un paisaje árido en un manto de colores Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Reparations can work when claims are grounded in solid evidence
item.description: At the Commonwealth summit in Antigua in November 2026, Britain's King Charles expressed sorrow for Britain's role in the slave trade. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stellar pulses reveal hidden binary in JWST calibration star sample
item.description: Stars used to calibrate the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) must have precisely characterized spectra so that their fluxes can be measured accurately. Yet some stars that appear single may in fact harbor unresolved companions that alter their predicted radiation. One such object, HD 158485—an A-type star in the JWST calibration program—has now been shown to be a binary system whose two stars both pulsate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
item.description: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Taveau

item.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%
item.description: https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-j... https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/nvidia-jensen-huang-congress... Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50611576 Points: 1586 # Comments: 2722 Publicado también por: Hacker News - Portada, Al Jazeera English, Ars Technica. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Discovery of curse ritual in trash dump surprises Egyptologist: 'It must have been widespread in ancient Egypt'
item.description: The discovery of 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in the ancient city of Thebes is changing researchers' understanding of one of ancient Egypt's most famous curse rituals. The fragments show that the ritual was probably far more widespread and commonplace than previously believed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A fungus that can survive in Chernobyl could help create materials that trap and break down nerve agents and pesticides
item.description: Deep inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone, where radiation levels have remained unsafe for people for the past 40 years, black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine. They're entirely undeterred by the radiation—in fact, some fungi even grow toward it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 310 million-year-old fossil reveals scorpion that looked much like modern relatives
item.description: As the month of Scorpio rolls over, Flinders University researchers have been taking a close look at a rare prehistoric scorpion. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Croatia and Costa Rica lead countries in sustainable development—while Norway ranks near bottom
item.description: Croatia and Costa Rica are the countries with the highest sustainable development in the world, as revealed by a new Sustainable Development Index (SDI) developed by researchers at ICTA-UAB. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study reveals how modern humans may have driven Neanderthals to extinction
item.description: The last of the Neanderthals died out in Europe around the same time that our own species, Homo sapiens, was spreading across the continent. Were these two events connected, or was it just a coincidence? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Star's record eruption shows how key elements can spread through space
item.description: An international team of astronomers led by Wouter Vlemmings and Miora Andriantsaralaza, both from Chalmers, have imaged a nearby star in unprecedented detail, using the telescope ALMA in Chile. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How DNA's surroundings shape gene regulation
item.description: Turning genes on and off requires transcription factors—proteins that bind specific stretches of DNA and help control gene activity. But DNA is not laid out bare inside the nucleus. It is wrapped around proteins and folded into chromatin, which can make some regions easier to reach than others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why are some people single—and what makes them happy? New research offers answers
item.description: Why do some people remain single while others find romantic partners? And does being single necessarily mean being less happy? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hidden leaf dynamics could improve Amazon rainforest carbon uptake estimates
item.description: From space, the Amazon rainforest looks like an unbroken expanse of green. But a new study conducted by researchers from the School of Biological Sciences at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), together with international collaborators, reveals seasonal leaf changes hidden within this seemingly constant canopy. Largely undetected by conventional satellite observations, these changes have significant implications for estimating the rainforest's carbon uptake. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When the upwelling failed, Panama's fish oil trade collapsed within months
item.description: A year after scientists at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI) in Panama reported the first recorded failure of the Gulf of Panama's seasonal upwelling, a follow-up study now documents how that failure moved through the system, from wind to plankton to fish to exports, using records that fishing companies rarely share. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Baltic Sea measurements reveal more complex ocean-atmosphere exchanges than previously assumed
item.description: Like humans, the ocean breathes. And when it does, a new study shows that far more is happening than researchers have previously assumed. "We can see that the ocean's chemical breathing is far more diverse and dynamic than we previously thought," says Mehrshad Foroughan, a postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Biology who is the first author of the new study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How shells are made: New insights elucidate crystals' uptake of 'disruptors'
item.description: For a mollusk to build its shell, it uses brittle chalk—crystalline calcite—which must take in other materials to make the chalk stronger. That process of incorporation has long been a mystery—one that Professor Lara Estroff has been working on for her entire career. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Microscopic chambers reveal how bacteria navigate tight spots
item.description: New York University researchers have built a way to observe bacteria as they typically live: in confinement. The research, published in the journal Small, introduces microscopic traps that mimic the tiny crevices where bacteria actually live—for instance, in soil or in our mouths. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study reveals dual roles for ATRX in nucleosome remodeling and histone chaperoning
item.description: ATRX is an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler that helps maintain genome stability. Mutations in ATRX cause ATR-X syndrome and are found in several types of cancer. ATRX is best known for working with the histone chaperone DAXX to deposit the histone variant H3.3 in heterochromatin, where it helps maintain gene silencing and chromatin integrity. However, how ATRX regulates its own ATPase activity, uses ATP to remodel nucleosomes and functions in accessible chromatin remains unclear. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: No magnets needed: Extreme voltage drives completely new kind of Hall effect
item.description: The Hall effect, a physical phenomenon in which a current arises perpendicular to a voltage applied across a material, has been of particular interest to physicists since it was discovered more than a century ago. Over time, physicists have broadened their understanding of the Hall effect, describing quantum and anomalous versions that appear under nonclassical conditions. Recently, Rice University's Qimiao Si published a paper in Physical Review Letters describing a new variant called the fully nonequilibrium response that once again expands how physicists understand the Hall effect. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Oxidative stress alters and 'clogs' grass pollen allergens, study finds
item.description: Medical experts suspect that high levels of air pollution exacerbate the symptoms of hay fever patients. Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz (MPIC) have now solved a chemical puzzle: When pollen allergens encounter peroxynitrite, the allergens undergo surprisingly systematic changes. New chemical groups are attached at specific exposed sites on the protein. In addition, it "glues" or links the allergens together. The findings are published in the journal Free Radical Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New modeling tool sheds light on how climate change could reshape marine ecosystems
item.description: A new high-resolution modeling tool is offering one of the clearest pictures yet of how climate change could affect a vital part of the marine food chain in Northwest European seas. The machine learning model developed by researchers at the University of Strathclyde predicts how zooplankton—tiny drifting animals that underpin marine ecosystems—could respond to changing ocean conditions over the coming decades. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New fiber laser combines ultrashort pulses with broad spectrum and stable output
item.description: Femtosecond lasers produce pulses lasting only quadrillionths of a second. Their speed makes them useful for imaging rapid processes, sampling high-frequency signals and measuring distance or time with high precision. For these applications, a laser must provide not only short pulses and a broad spectrum but also stable output. Fluctuations in pulse intensity or timing can reduce image quality and measurement accuracy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bacteria split their membranes to kill infected cells and block viral spread, study shows
item.description: A new study reveals a previously unknown bacterial immune mechanism in which the signaling molecule 2′,3′-cGAMP triggers the splitting of the bacterial membrane into two distinct bilayers, leading to the death of infected cells and preventing further phage propagation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Significance and stats: Massive sample sizes do not guarantee reliable findings, study suggests
item.description: The increasing use of large health care databases has exposed a fundamental statistical weakness: the assumption that bigger data sets automatically produce more reliable findings. A review of a large health care database associated with vaccination and cancer in the International Journal of Medical Engineering and Informatics shows that in practice, standard statistical methods can generate misleading levels of significance, masking underlying flaws in the data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Countries agree on new ways to achieve safe chemical use
item.description: Countries have agreed on new measures to speed up efforts aimed at preventing the harmful effects of chemical products on health and the environment, the U.N. said. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Proteins with ancient viral roots guard genetic switches left by mobile DNA
item.description: Much of our genome contains mobile pieces or "transposable elements": pieces of DNA that spread and accumulated over millions of years, some originating from ancient viruses. Although many are no longer mobile, their sequences can influence when nearby genes switch on or off. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study reveals surge-detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in Pamir Mountains
item.description: Researchers have reconstructed a surge–detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan, revealing how a period of rapid glacier acceleration culminated in two successive large-scale ice-detachment events. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How self-perception influences the way women view sexualized images
item.description: Women are frequently sexualized in the media, which leads to their widespread objectification in society and worsens their mental health on a large scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: On Yelp, actions speak louder than words, study reveals
item.description: As artificial intelligence makes it easier to pump out convincing reviews for restaurants and travel accommodations, a new study from the University of Massachusetts Amherst suggests a better clue to uncovering suspect reviews isn't the writing—it's the posting habits. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How Antarctica helped to set Earth's hottest day on record
item.description: Rivers in the sky bringing moisture to Antarctica during the Southern Hemisphere winter help explain short-term peaks in the world's average temperature, new research has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
item.description: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
item.description: NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: David Lam

item.title: Cop31 collapses: why did climate talks fall apart? - The Latest
item.description: Countries at the Cop31 climate summit failed to reach a keystone agreement for the first time in 17 years. The talks, co-chaired by Turkey and Australia, were intended to produce a pact that would have injected urgency into climate action and financing for vulnerable states. Instead, the deal failed after a standoff over fossil fuels and support for countries exposed to the climate crisis. Guardian Australia’s climate and environment reporter Graham Readfearn tells Lucy Hough why there are calls for urgent reform of the Cop process – watch on YouTube Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Presented by Lucy Houghwith Graham Readfearn; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Leonore Schick; executive producer Zoe Hitch

item.title: El fracaso de la COP31 acelera los llamados a reformar la toma de decisiones sobre la crisis climática
item.description: La falta de un acuerdo político tras 48 horas de negociaciones, prolongadas más que nunca, dio paso a fuertes críticas y reacciones de líderes políticos, naciones vulnerables y de defensores y activistas del clima. El veto de las naciones productoras de combustibles fósiles —Arabia Saudita, Rusia e India, principalmente— a una declaración que hiciera mención a la transición energética ha encendido los llamados a reformar el mecanismo para la toma de decisiones basado en el consenso. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: NASA+ Documentary Captures Europa Clipper’s Journey Into Deep Space
item.description: NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.” The documentary will air on NASA+, the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Barnett

item.title: Behind COP31 failure: A showdown over fossil fuel interests
item.description: Several countries and environmental groups expressed fury at the collapse of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey on Sunday, amid a dramatic failure to thrash out an agreement, two days after the summit was scheduled to end. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels – the root cause of the climate crisis – with the EU then refusing to back a weakened text. Our Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Valérie DEKIMPE

item.title: COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance
item.description: COP31 ended without a consensus deal for the first time since 2009. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Bob Berwyn, Inside Climate News

item.title: NASA’s Webb Shows How Supernova Dust Chronicles Star Evolution
item.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. This high-resolution, mid-infrared observation from Webb […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Domestic violence perpetrators are using smart car features to abuse, researchers warn
item.description: Exclusive: Alarming report reveals how tracking and monitoring functions and digital key access have been used to facilitate abuse Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Earlier this year a man in Australia was found guilty of using a connected car app to harass his former partner, including restricting the speed at which she could drive, sometimes to 40km an hour . In 2022 in the US, a woman found her former husband had used a car app associated with her car to track her; the carmaker then allegedly refused to terminate the former partner’s digital access to the… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Jordyn Beazley

item.title: ‘Worst COP ever’: Climate talks collapse after draft deal fails to include fossil fuels
item.description: Governments and campaigners rejected the "cover decision" drafted at the U.N.'s climate summit, COP31, on Sunday. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: En 1976 los arqueólogos excavaron una casa romana en Mérida. Ahora unos estudiantes han descubierto el tesoro que ocultaba
item.description: Ha tardado medio siglo en conseguirlo, pero la Huerta de Otero acaba de ganarse un lugar destacado en el mapa arqueológico español. Dio un primer paso para lograrlo en el verano de 2023 , cuando los investigadores desenterraron allí un fascinante mosaico policromo de 30 m2; y ha vuelto a hacerlo ahora, con el anuncio de otro descubrimiento de calado: una serie de pinturas murales muy bien conservadas que muestran temas mitológicos, plantas y animales. Ambos hallazgos nos hablan de la relevancia de una opulenta domus romana que probablemente estuvo habitada hacia los siglos I y V d.C. y que… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Prego

item.title: Huge planet, tiny star: discovery challenges textbook view of how giants form
item.description: Chinese and American astronomers have found a planet nearly five times the mass of Jupiter circling a small, dim star, challenging the textbook view of how giant planets form and how many of them are out there. The team, from Carnegie Science in Washington and Shanghai Jiao Tong and Tsinghua universities, spotted the planet – known as HIP 88962 b – with the Magellan Clay Telescope in Chile after 16 years of observations. Its host star has only two-thirds the mass of our sun – too small to build... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good
item.description: Researchers in Japan have developed an innovative gum disease treatment that uses egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light to destroy harmful bacteria without harming beneficial microbes. Unlike conventional treatments, the approach preserves the mouth's natural bacterial balance and protects healthy gum cells. In mice, it significantly reduced the bone loss associated with periodontitis, a major cause of tooth loss. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way
item.description: A surprising discovery suggests the Milky Way may be making stars in places where most galaxies cannot. Scientists found evidence that a massive rotating structure near the galactic center is creating powerful shock waves that trigger star formation rather than suppress it. Even more unexpectedly, part of the Norma spiral arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a vast region where new stars are being born. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation
item.description: Astronomers have discovered the oldest known compact pair of quasars, powered by two enormous black holes that existed just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Weighing an astonishing 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, these cosmic giants somehow grew to incredible sizes far earlier than current theories can explain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Mysterious new viruses reveal a missing link in evolution
item.description: Scientists have discovered previously unknown viruses that could help explain how some of life’s earliest biological structures evolved. The surprising findings challenge a longstanding evolutionary theory and suggest that viruses may have hidden capabilities far beyond simply infecting cells. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover that leukemia can begin developing 50 years before diagnosis
item.description: A groundbreaking study reveals that acute myeloid leukemia (AML), an aggressive blood cancer, can begin developing more than 50 years before diagnosis, with the first cancer-driving mutation appearing before age 20 in two-thirds of cases. Scientists discovered that these mutated cells grow in surprisingly predictable patterns, accelerating dramatically as additional mutations accumulate. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: COP31 ends without agreement as divisions deepen over fossil fuels
item.description: UN climate chief Simon Stiell expressed disappointment over the outcome, warning that the failure to secure agreement on key presidency-led decisions must not be repeated. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com

item.title: Hidden for 100 million years: X-rays reveal an ancient flower from the age of dinosaurs
item.description: In a new paper published in the American Journal of Botany, a team of scientists from the U.S. and UK reveal an incredible fossil from the mid-Cretaceous period (around 100 million years ago), opening up a new window into the early evolutionary history of modern-day plants. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds Tasmania farmland plantations reach just 33-43% of forest scores
item.description: Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman
item.description: Archaeologists have uncovered evidence that Verica, the Iron Age ruler whose exile helped trigger Rome’s invasion of Britain in AD 43, was actually a woman. The discovery challenges centuries of historical assumptions and suggests that a largely forgotten female leader may have changed the course of British history. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 23 – The Emergence of Dark Nebula Lynds 1251

item.description: Black rats can be difficult to trap, but a common marketing tactic in shops and restaurants increases capture rates, a new study shows. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
item.description: A next-generation geodetic instrument developed by NASA, part of a network that helps measure satellites’ orbits and the planet’s shape, has debuted in Svalbard, Norway. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Robot submarine exploring world's deepest ocean trench finds unprecedented volcanic activity
item.description: Fifty-two million years ago, the Pacific tectonic plate began to slide under the Philippine Sea plate, forming the Mariana Trench, the deepest known valley on the Earth's ocean floor. The deepest part of this abyss, the Challenger Deep, is almost 11,000 meters (36,000 feet) below sea level. But why is it so deep? Scientists trying to answer this question sent a remotely operated vehicle to collect samples around the Deep, where they found evidence of the world's deepest underwater explosive volcanic eruptions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
item.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50% larger than a human’s
item.description: A tiny California trapdoor spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome roughly 50% larger than a human's, despite being only about the size of a quarter. Scientists discovered that its enormous genome contains 4.6 billion DNA base pairs and 52 chromosomes, revealing surprising clues about spider evolution. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Mice slept 70% less after scientists switched off these brain cells
item.description: Scientists have discovered brain cells that actively generate the irresistible urge to sleep, and shutting them down allowed mice to sleep 70% less than normal. Remarkably, many of the animals avoided the severe behavioral consequences of sleep deprivation, raising intriguing possibilities for future sleep research. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status after 25 years as vaccine myths persist
item.description: The United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years, and a new survey reveals widespread misconceptions about the deadly disease and its vaccine. With measles cases surging, more than one-third of Americans still believe or are uncertain about the debunked vaccine-autism link, while most don't know the disease's risks or how many vaccine doses children need. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between weak bones and faster brain aging
item.description: Weakening bones may reveal more about brain health than scientists previously realized, with new research linking lower spinal bone density to faster cognitive decline and accelerated changes in the brain's white matter. The surprising connection suggests that routine medical scans could help uncover hidden warning signs of brain aging and identify people at increased risk of dementia. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapse
item.description: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is taking place amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the war in Iran. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Climate talks crash a sign of anger with oil lobby, scientist says
item.description: Countries have rejected a climate deal that ignores fossil fuels, but experts say that reflects anger rather than indifference. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Reliance on technology is eroding trust in one another and ability to tell what is even real, expert warns
item.description: The danger of generative AI is not some distant algorithmic failure; it is the slow erosion of our ability to tell what's real, to trust our institutions and to think for ourselves at all. These are the warnings of Mateusz Łabuz in his new book, The End of Reality. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A new snake found near the China-Nepal border looks like an earthworm
item.description: A new species of blind snake named Indotyphlops gyirongensis has been identified in Gyirong County, China. The specimen was found at a high elevation under a stone in August 2025. This snake is adapted to a life underground and has several unique physical traits. Researchers used both physical examination and genetic analysis to establish its distinct lineage. Further studies are needed to understand its distribution, population, and dietary habits. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years
item.description: Medications taken years or even long ago may leave lasting changes in your gut microbiome, according to a study of more than 2,500 people. Researchers discovered that common drugs, including antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, can leave microbial “fingerprints” long after patients stop taking them. Surprisingly, some anxiety medications had effects comparable to broad-spectrum antibiotics. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds
item.description: People with type 2 diabetes face a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease, according to a major new review of 40 studies. Researchers estimate that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year. By focusing specifically on these two conditions, the study offers a clearer understanding of a potentially serious connection between metabolic health and brain health. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Tras ocho años de viaje, la sonda BepiColombo llega a la órbita de Mercurio
item.description: La Agencia Espacial Europea (ESA) anunció este domingo 22 de noviembre que la sonda doble europea y japonesa BepiColombo logró entrar en la órbita de Mercurio, después de ocho años de viaje. Mercurio es el planeta más pequeño del sistema solar y el menos conocido. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: Silver briefly forms a rare crystal structure seen in radioactive polonium
item.description: How atoms are arranged in a material shapes many of its properties. The same carbon atoms, for example, can form diamond and graphite depending on how they are arranged, giving rise to materials with vastly different chemical and physical properties. Now, researchers at Hokkaido University have discovered a new crystal structure of silver with unusually high chemical reactivity. The findings, published in Nano Letters, could open new avenues for exploring materials with desirable properties. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Fossil fuels are at the centre of deep division. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.description: La COP31 en Antalya culminó sin consenso luego de que varias delegaciones objetaran un borrador que omitía el abandono de los hidrocarburos. El desenlace provocó fuertes cuestionamientos de la Unión Europea y del secretario general António Guterres tras dos jornadas de intensas prórrogas. Publicado también por: La Nación - El Mundo. item.description: For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: COP31 negotiations break down as countries fail to agree on climate deal
item.description: A fight over whether to mention fossil fuels caused the talks, which had become the longest in summit history, to fall apart. It was the first such collapse in over a decade. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.

item.title: A firefly not seen since 1983 has been found again after scientist recognised its amber flashes
item.description: Exciting news emerged in 2026 when a firefly, thought to have vanished since 1983, was rediscovered in Delaware and Virginia. Its unique amber flash patterns caught the attention of researchers, confirming its survival. Habitat loss is suspected to have led to its absence from earlier records. Community engagement significantly aided in this rediscovery, prompting further surveys to assess the firefly's population and habitat requirements. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: A research team has quantified an important component of the global nitrogen cycle. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find 156-million-year-old horned reptile fossil in Wyoming sandstone
item.description: A remarkable discovery in Wyoming has unearthed a fossil of a diminutive dinosaur-like creature, dating back 156 million years to the Jurassic era. Advanced imaging techniques uncovered this skeleton entombed in sandstone. Researchers classify it as an early reptilian branch, enhancing our understanding of evolutionary history. Analysis indicates it inhabited freshwater environments and may have fallen prey to a larger predator. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: JWST finds a possible black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy in the early universe
item.description: How the first massive black holes formed in the universe remains an open question in astronomy. Black holes weighing about a billion solar masses within the first billion years of the universe require extraordinary origin stories. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global… Publicado también por: ABC News Australia. item.title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
item.description: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet's mountain of mysteries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
item.description: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat Sunday after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hybrid nanocrystal surface reveals new way to tune interactions with infrared light
item.description: A one-crystal-thick sheet made from two types of nanocrystals mixed in solution can amplify or suppress infrared light beyond the sum of its parts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La Cumbre del Clima de la ONU fracasó en llegar a un acuerdo por el uso de los combustibles fósiles
item.description: La Unión Europea, Panamá, las Islas Marshall y otros países rechazaron el borrador del acuerdo final de la COP31 porque no incluye ninguna referencia a los combustibles fósiles ni a la transición para abandonar su uso. Tras más de 44 horas de prórroga, las negociaciones continúan estancadas y la cumbre corre el riesgo de concluir sin un acuerdo definitivo. Nuestro corresponsal, Adrià Rocha, nos amplía la información. Publicado también por: France 24 - Español, Clarín - Mundo. Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.
